summary: No proposals today. Cash is $64.78 against a 10% buffer of $62.61, so only about $2 can go into new buys, and L4 rules out a buy that small. The account is 89.65% invested, at the top of the target range, and the Market Analyst is risk-off and asks for small new sizing ahead of Nvidia's 11-17 print. Held-book review (L7), done from each stop block and qualitative clause: no stop is tripped. BND (mark 71.10 vs stop 70.00) and IEF (90.94 vs 89.50) are flagged NEAR, both 1.6% above their stops. BND's clause needs the Market Analyst to be risk-on, and he is risk-off; TLT is 2.23% and IEF 1.31% below their 200-day averages, both short of the 3% trigger. IEF is 1.31% below its 200-day, short of 3%. VNQ's clause needs TLT more than 3% below its 200-day, and it is 2.23%; Real Estate is not on the avoid list, though the Market Analyst now rates VNQ hold-not-add. VOO and VTI: SPY 759.81 is above the 200-day SMA the regime filter computes (728.65 as of 11-11; the stored 728.3 is stale and is the PM's to restate), and RSP 21d is +4.38%. WMT: close 125.67 vs stop 116, and XLP 21d is +8.62%, above the +3% line. CARG, MSCI and VRSN have no guidance cut or negative 8-K, and DPZ has no confirmed guidance cut (News Analyst: no 4.01, 4.02 or 5.02 on any holding). KR's cyber clause and INCY's guidance-cut and trial-failure clauses are not tripped. FAST has no new report. The IDXX-vs-XLV and INCY-vs-XLV clauses still can't be checked because neither stock's 21-day return is in the packet (L6). INCY's stop text still measures from the 11-10 close instead of the $119.37 fill, which is for the PM's thesis_updates. I considered trimming WMT, now 12.0% of equity going into an estimated, unconfirmed 11-19 print inside the 5-day window, with crowded PT raises. I did not propose it. Consumer Staples is a Market Analyst favored sector, WMT's beta is about zero in a risk-off tape, and the print risk cuts both ways. The PM should still weigh the gap risk that its own L7 note raised. No sector claims were made (L3), and the earnings dates come from the News Analyst's per-name filing checks (L2).
